name: Epiblepharon

criteria.description: Presence of a redundant horizontal skin fold overriding the eyelid margin
Inward rotation of eyelashes causing contact with the ocular surface
Signs of ocular surface irritation such as conjunctival injection or keratitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of redundant eyelid skin fold with inwardly directed eyelashes causing ocular surface contact
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; slit-lamp examination may assist in assessing corneal involvement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Redundant horizontal skin fold on lower eyelid
searchTerms: extra horizontal skin fold on lower eyelid

pathognomonic.symptomName: Inward rotation of lower eyelid eyelashes (ciliary misdirection)

common.symptomName: Ocular surface irritation due to eyelash-corneal contact
searchTerms: eye irritation from lashes touching cornea
ocular discomfort due to eyelash contact

occasional.symptomName: Foreign body sensation in the eye
Corneal neovascularization secondary to chronic irritation

rare.symptomName: Visual impairment due to corneal scarring
searchTerms: impaired eyesight due to corneal damage

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing eyelash-corneal contact and corneal epithelial changes
genetic: No established genetic mutation; likely multifactorial with ethnic predisposition
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic eyelid fold and lash misdirection

distinguishingFeatures: Inward turning of eyelid margin itself rather than redundant skin fold
Eyelid margin inversion rather than skin fold
Misplaced eyelashes without redundant skin fold
Usually secondary to inflammation or scarring

redFlags: Corneal ulceration or persistent epithelial defect
Visual impairment or decreased visual acuity
Secondary bacterial infection of the ocular surface
references: Kang S, et al. Epiblepharon in East Asian children: clinical features and surgical outcomes. J Pediatr Ophthalmol Strabismus. 2018.
American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Patterns: Eyelid Disorders, 2020
